title: Company-wide policies and processes - access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Priya Nair
body:
Overview

This page centralizes Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard processes for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and the canonical internal templates used across teams. It provides policy statements, ownership, step‑by‑step procedures, approval thresholds, and links to templates and related pages. Teams should follow these procedures for all applicable requests; deviations require documented approval from the owner_team.

1) Access and Permissions

Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access to systems and data while enabling teams to get productive quickly.

Scope: Applies to employee, contractor, and vendor access for all Redwood production and internal systems.

Policy highlights:
- Access is role-based and granted using the principle of least privilege.
- Privileged access (sudo, database root, production cluster ownership) requires Security approval and two-step attestations.
- All access requests and changes must be recorded in the access ticketing project (Jira: INFRA-ACC).

Request process:
1. Employee/manager opens an INFRA-ACC request with: requested resources, justification, duration (if temporary), and approver.
2. Manager approval (auto-escalates after 3 business days).
3. For privileged requests, Security reviews and must approve within 48 hours.
4. IAM automation applies the least-privilege role and adds the request to quarterly attestation lists.

Approval matrix (summary):
| Resource category | Approver | Threshold |
|---|---:|---:|
| Non-prod infra (read) | Manager | immediate |
| Prod infra (write) | Manager + Service Owner | requires justification |
| Privileged (DB root, SRE admin) | Manager + Security | documented justification + training |

Periodic reviews and revocation:
- Team owners must complete an access attestation every quarter. Non-attested access will be revoked after 30 days.
- Automated alerts for inactive accounts (90 days) are sent to managers.

Emergency access:
- Emergency (break-glass) access is handled through the on-call Security SRE rotation. Requests must include timespan and purpose and are logged for post-hoc review.

2) Change Management

Objective: Minimize risk and customer impact from changes to production systems while enabling rapid iteration.

Change types:
- Standard change: pre-authorized, low-risk (e.g., routine config updates). No CAB approval required if within standard template.
- Normal change: requires change request (CR) and CAB review.
- Major change: high risk or customer-impacting; requires stakeholder sign-off and scheduled maintenance window.
- Emergency change: used to remediate incidents; documented and reviewed after the fact.

Process (normal change):
1. Create a Change Request (Confluence change request template + Jira CR ticket). Include scope, rollback plan, test plan, owner, schedule, and impact.
2. Submit to Change Advisory Board (CAB) 72 hours before proposed window. CAB reviews for conflicts and risk.
3. Obtain approvals from Service Owner, Platform Lead, and SRE.
4. Execute during approved maintenance window.
5. Post-change verification and update runbooks.

Rollbacks & metrics:
- Every CR must include a clear rollback plan and success criteria.
- Changes that increase incident rate or SLO error budget consumption by >10% trigger an immediate review.

Scheduled maintenance windows:
- Weekdays: 02:00–05:00 UTC (low traffic). Critical customer-impact changes require business stakeholder coordination.

3) Data Management

Purpose: Protect customer and company data with clear classification, retention, access, and handling rules.

Data classification:
- PUBLIC: information intended for public release.
- INTERNAL: company operational info; not customer-sensitive.
- CONFIDENTIAL: contains customer data, PII, or business-sensitive material.
- RESTRICTED: regulated or high-risk data (HIPAA, payment data).

Handling rules:
- CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED must be encrypted at rest and in transit (TLS 1.2+). Key management must use company KMS (cloud KMS or HSM for Private deployments).
- Production datasets must be masked/anonymized for non-prod use.
- Access to CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED data requires Security approval and a documented business justification.

Retention & deletion:
- Default retention: logs 30 days, metrics 365 days, customer backups 7 years (subject to contractual terms).
- Data deletion requests (e.g., subject access or right-to-erasure) should be submitted to privacy@redwood.com and routed through Legal + Security.

Backups and recovery:
- Daily backups for critical datasets with weekly test restores. Restore runbooks live in eng-infra/runbooks.

Audit & monitoring:
- Access to sensitive data is logged and retained for at least 1 year. Security runs quarterly audits; exceptions documented in risk-and-exceptions.

4) Procurement and Expenses

Objective: Ensure cost control, vendor compliance, and predictable purchasing while empowering teams to buy required services.

Procurement thresholds & approvals:
| Amount (USD) | Approval required | Notes |
|---:|---|---|
| Up to $2,500 | Manager | Use corporate card or expense report |
| $2,501 - $25,000 | Manager + Finance | Preferred vendor list encouraged |
| > $25,000 | Manager + Finance + Legal | PO required; procurement coordinates RFP if needed |

Process steps for purchases > $2,500:
1. Submit Procurement Request form (template link below) with justification, vendor, and budget code.
2. Finance reviews for budget and vendor status within 3 business days.
3. Legal reviews contracts > $25k or with data-processing implications.
4. Procurement issues PO and confirms delivery/acceptance.

Expenses & corporate card policy:
- Employees must submit receipts within 14 days. Meals and incidental per diem follow the published reimbursement rates.
- Corporate cards: issued upon manager request; misuse will result in revocation and possible disciplinary action.

5) Vendor Management

Objective: Manage third-party risk and ensure contractual and security expectations are met.

Onboarding checklist (vendor onboarding template):
- Vendor contact & SOC/attestation (SOC2, ISO27001) or completed Security Questionnaire (SIG-lite).
- Data processing agreement (DPA) for vendors handling customer data.
- Contract owner assigned (must be a full-time Redwood employee).
- Payment/PO setup and vendor classification.

Ongoing monitoring:
- Annual vendor review for critical vendors; triage findings into remediation plans.
- Security assessments for vendors with access to CONFIDENTIAL or RESTRICTED data.

Termination & offboarding:
- Ensure return or certified destruction of company data. Revoke access, remove from billing, and confirm final invoices.

6) Travel Policy

Scope: Business travel for employees and contractors.

Pre-approval & booking:
- All international travel requires manager and People Ops pre-approval. Use the Travel Request template.
- Preferred booking channels (corporate travel portal) must be used for flights > $1,000 or multi-leg itineraries.

Expenses and per diem:
- Reimbursable expenses: airfare (economy unless pre-approved), lodging (mid-range hotels), ground transportation, meals, and conference fees.
- Receipts are required for all reimbursements. Submit within 14 days of trip end.

Travel safety:
- Employees traveling to high-risk regions must register with People Ops and Security and complete pre-travel security briefing.
- Emergency contact and travel insurance details must be recorded in the Travel Request.

7) Internal Templates and Examples

Canonical templates (links):
- Access Request template: /confluence/templates/access-request
- Change Request template: /confluence/templates/change-request
- Procurement Request form: /confluence/templates/procurement-request
- Vendor Onboarding checklist: /confluence/templates/vendor-onboarding
- Travel Request template: /confluence/templates/travel-request

Example: Change Request summary fields (recommended)
- Title
- Owner
- Service(s) impacted
- Proposed window
- Risk level
- Rollback plan (step-by-step)
- Test/verification plan

Ownership and escalation
- Policy owner: people-ops (Priya Nair).
- Security owner (data & access): Security (Maya Zhou).
- Procurement owner: Finance (Ethan Clark).
- For urgent clarifications, open a slack channel #policy-questions and tag the owner_team.

Exceptions and amendments
- Requests for exceptions should be submitted to risk-and-exceptions with documented compensating controls. Exceptions expire after the approved period and must be renewed.
